title: Per-tenant routing recommender and guarded apply for batching/cache policies
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Background: We need an automated recommendation engine that suggests batching and KV-cache config deltas at the per-tenant and per-route granularity, plus a guarded/staged apply path that minimizes customer impact and enables automatic rollback when regressions are detected. Current manual tuning is slow, error-prone, and lacks a safe automation surface for non-platform engineers.

Scope:
- Build a recommender that consumes historical telemetry (latency distribution, p95/p99, token counts, request concurrency, cache hit rates) and outputs per-tenant/per-route candidate changes: batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, prefix_cache_enabled, cache_ttl, and routing tier (fast/standard/cheap).
- Attach a safety profile to each recommendation: allowlist/denylist, tier constraints (e.g., enterprise tenants cannot be auto-downgraded), and cost delta + latency risk estimate.
- Implement a guarded-apply pipeline: dry-run/simulate -> staged canary -> observability gates -> auto-fallback/rollback.
- Integrate with Console to surface recommendations, enable reviewer approvals, and kick off the staged apply.
- Provide a runbook and automated rollback actions when metrics cross abort thresholds.

Non-goals:
- Replacing manual policy authoring UI in Console (that remains separate).
- Making the recommender the single source of truth for global policies; recommendations must be reviewable.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Recommender model: lightweight heuristic + rules engine initially (fast iteration), with a telemetry-driven scoring function that estimates cost savings and latency/regression risk. ML model deferred to next quarter.
- Safety-first defaults: recommendations are opt-in for P0/P1 customers and opt-out for enterprise tier; auto-apply only allowed for P2/P3 tiers after explicit system opt-in.
- Canary cadence: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows per step. Abort if p95 increases > 15% or error-rate up > 0.5% absolute or cache hit-rate drops > 10% relative.
- Allowlist/denylist: per-tenant denylist to block auto-apply; route-level allowlist to enable aggressive batching on safe routes.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Recommender can run a historical simulation (dry-run) producing per-tenant+route suggestions and an estimated unit-cost delta.
2) Console shows recommendations with safety profile and an "Initiate guarded apply" button for reviewers.
3) Guarded apply executes staged canary with automated gating and will automatically rollback when any abort condition is met.
4) Runbook and a one-click rollback are available in the event of a manual abort.
5) Telemetry dashboard displays pre/post comparisons for cost, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, and cache hit-rate for every canary step.

Telemetry and metrics to capture:
- Per-tenant per-route: requests/sec, tokens/sec, avg token latency, p95/p99 latency, error-rate (4xx/5xx breakdown), batch sizes distribution, cache hits/misses, and cost-per-token estimate.
- Recommendation metrics: count accepted, rejected, auto-applied, rolled back, estimated savings realized.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement recommender dry-run pipeline and simulation UI (backend + Console read-only view).
- Week 2: Implement allowlist/denylist + tier-based gating logic.
- Week 3: Implement the guarded-apply executor with canary orchestration and observable hooks.
- Week 4: Run staged tests in staging with synthetic workloads and a small set of opt-in internal tenants.
- Week 5: Soft launch to P2/P3 customers, monitor dashboards, collect feedback.

Abort and rollback policy:
- Automated abort triggers if any canary step violates thresholds. On abort, the system will: mark the recommendation failed, roll back config to pre-change version, annotate the ticket and send alerts to on-call and the recommender owners.
- Manual abort: reviewers can manually abort from Console which triggers immediate rollback and captures state for postmortem.

Safety mitigations:
- Per-tenant immutable denylist for high-risk/regulatory customers.
- Enterprise tier protection: no auto-apply without explicit legal/CS consent.
- Preflight simulation (dry-run) must run and show no >10% p95 delta before any staged canary.
- Canary windows and minimum sample sizes to avoid noisy metrics.
